answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to one real cedar-shingled boathouse roof in a working harbor, where the keeper climbs a spiral stair each season to replace shingles under a licensed roofer's inspection. Random spot-checks summon the holder to their own roof within a day, and one person cannot roof two boathouses at once. The registration fee in outside money doubles per further identity on the same funding trail, so each extra fake costs another real roof, another season of labor, another human, and twice the prior fee.
